modules.description: A virtual machine on a libvirt/QEMU host: provision a batch, tear one down, resize it, or read the inventory.
modules.name: vm

created.description:
Provision `count` VMs and wait until every one of them is ready.
Idempotent on the batch identity: a rerun adopts the domains it already
made (matched by the domain metadata label `soulstack-run`, or by the
name `<name>-<seq>`) and tops up only what is missing, at the first free
indexes.
Each VM boots from a qcow2 overlay on the profile's image and a NoCloud
seed carrying `userdata`; ready means the guest took a DHCP lease and
reported a hostname, which is where sid and primary_ip come from.
Output.hosts is the provisioned batch, one entry per VM:
{vm_id, sid, primary_ip, state, attributes}, where attributes is
{namespace, name, cpu_size, ram_size, image_id, network_id, created_at, run_label}.
A VM that did not come up is a bare {vm_id} and the step reports failed.
It does NOT carry bootstrap_token — minting one needs the Keeper's token
store, which a plugin has no access to.
No dry-run preview.

count.description: How many VMs the batch holds. The scan counts what already exists, so this is the TOTAL, not the number to add.

endpoint.description: libvirt connection URI — e.g. qemu:///system, or qemu+ssh://host/system for a remote hypervisor.

name.description: Batch identity: domains are named `<name>-<seq>` and labelled with it. Required unless profile.labels["soulstack-run"] is set — without one of the two a rerun cannot recognise its own domains and would spawn orphans.

namespace.description: Scope label stamped into domain metadata. It is what keeps this artifact away from VMs it did not create: `probed` and `destroyed` see nothing outside it. Required on every action but `created`, where profile.namespace may supply it.

profile.description: The VM spec — a CLOSED set of fields; an unrecognised key is refused rather than ignored. namespace (the placement scope, winning over the step's), network_id (UUID of a libvirt network), cpu_size (cores), ram_size and boot_disk_size (BYTES), and the image as EITHER image_id (a UUID derived from the volume name) OR image_name (a volume in the image pool, e.g. debian-12). Optional: boot_disk_name, deletion_protection, labels.

userdata.description: cloud-init user-data, at most 32 KiB. The cap bounds what goes onto the NoCloud seed; a document that large is a rendering accident rather than an intention.

destroyed.description:
Delete every VM in `vm_ids` and CONFIRM the teardown by polling.
A domain that is still being defined can refuse to go; the delete is
re-issued until the domain and its volumes are gone. A teardown that
could not be confirmed is reported failed, with the vm_id, never as
success. A domain carrying deletion_protection is refused.
Output.hosts is one {vm_id} per id addressed.
No dry-run preview.

endpoint.description: libvirt connection URI — e.g. qemu:///system, or qemu+ssh://host/system for a remote hypervisor.

namespace.description: Scope label stamped into domain metadata. It is what keeps this artifact away from VMs it did not create: `probed` and `destroyed` see nothing outside it. Required on every action but `created`, where profile.namespace may supply it.

vm_ids.description: Domain UUIDs to tear down. A VM that is already gone is an idempotent success.

probed.description:
Read the VM inventory of a namespace. Read-only, changed=false by
design (a probe, not a mutation): it creates, deletes and modifies
nothing. Only domains this artifact made are reported — the namespace
label is the scope, so an unrelated VM on the same host is invisible
here and untouchable by `destroyed`. Output.hosts has the same
{vm_id, sid, primary_ip, state, attributes} shape `created` produces,
attributes being
{namespace, name, cpu_size, ram_size, image_id, network_id, created_at, run_label}.
No dry-run preview.

endpoint.description: libvirt connection URI — e.g. qemu:///system, or qemu+ssh://host/system for a remote hypervisor.

namespace.description: Scope label stamped into domain metadata. It is what keeps this artifact away from VMs it did not create: `probed` and `destroyed` see nothing outside it. Required on every action but `created`, where profile.namespace may supply it.

run_label.description: Report only VMs carrying this value in the domain metadata label `soulstack-run` — the batch identity `created` stamps. Ignored when vm_ids is set.

vm_ids.description: Report only these domain UUIDs. Omitted, the whole namespace is listed (optionally narrowed by run_label).

resized.description:
Resize every VM in `vm_ids` to an ABSOLUTE target.
Disk grows online through a block resize (never shrinks — a target at or
below the current size is an idempotent skip); the guest filesystem
follows only if it runs growpart. cpu/ram go through
stop → update → start and therefore need allow_downtime; libvirt could
hot-plug some of that and this does not, so the consent the param asks
for is consent the operation actually spends.
The host's free memory and the disk pool's free space are prechecked
against the batch's summed positive delta: it fails closed, before any
VM is touched.
Output.results is one {vm_id, changed, caused_downtime, error?} per VM —
every VM is attempted, so a batch reports per-machine outcomes rather
than stopping at the first failure.
No dry-run preview.

allow_downtime.description: EXPLICIT consent to stop and start the VM. Required for a cpu/ram change and refused up front without it, so a batch never ends up half-stopped. A disk-only resize is online and does not need it.

cpu_cores.description: Target vCPU count. 0 leaves cpu alone.

disk_gb.description: Target boot-disk size in GiB. 0 leaves the disk alone. Shrinking is refused as an idempotent skip.

endpoint.description: libvirt connection URI — e.g. qemu:///system, or qemu+ssh://host/system for a remote hypervisor.

namespace.description: Scope label stamped into domain metadata. It is what keeps this artifact away from VMs it did not create: `probed` and `destroyed` see nothing outside it. Required on every action but `created`, where profile.namespace may supply it.

ram_mb.description: Target RAM in MiB. 0 leaves ram alone.

vm_ids.description: Domain UUIDs to resize. Every VM in the batch gets the same target.
